--- lecture: "03a" metadata-files: - ../../_slide-settings.yml format: revealjs: theme: default --- ::: {.my-title} # [Foundations of]{.my-subtitle}
[Data Science]{.blue} ::: {.my-grey} [{{< meta semester >}} | {{< meta course >}}]{}
[Jeffrey M. Girard | Lecture {{< meta lecture >}}]{} ::: ![](../../img/proud_coder_357EDD.svg){.absolute bottom=30 right=0 width="400"} ::: ## Roadmap ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column width="60%"} 1. Store reusable data in named objects using assignment (`<-`) 2. Transform data and objects using one or more functions ::: ::: {.column .tc .pv4 width="40%"} {{< lif "../../icons/map.json" trigger=hover colors=secondary:#2a76dd class=rc >}} ::: ::: # Assignment ## Assignment {.fs70} ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column width="60%"} - It is often useful to store data in [named objects]{.b .green} - This makes the data easier to use and re-use - This makes the code easier to write and read ::: {.fragment .mt1} - Which command is easier to follow? 1. Dial *7 8 5 8 6 4 0 8 4 1* 2. Call *Office Phone* ::: ::: {.fragment .mt1} - Named objects are created using [assignment]{.b .blue} - Give a **name** then an **arrow** then the **data** ::: ::: ::: {.column .tc .pv5 width="40%"} {{< lif "../../icons/contacts.json" trigger=hover colors=secondary:#2a76dd class=rc >}} ::: {.fragment} `office <- 7858640841` ::: ::: ::: ## Naming {.fs70} ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column width="60%"} - Object names can [only include]{.b .blue}: - Letters: `a-Z` - Numbers: `0-9` - Underscores: `_` - Periods: `.` ::: {.fragment .mt1} - Additional Rules: - Must [start with a letter or period]{.b .blue} - Cannot contain spaces or dashes - Cannot contain other symbols - Names are case-sensitive (`age` ≠ `Age`) ::: ::: ::: {.column .tc .pv5 width="40%"} {{< lif "../../icons/visa.json" trigger=hover colors=secondary:#2a76dd class=rc >}} ::: ::: ## Basic Assignment ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # x gets 2, print x x <- 2 x ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 2 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Make y from x, print y y <- 3 * x y ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 6 ``` ::: ::: ## Updating Objects ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Using x will not update it x + 1 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 3 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # x is still 2 x ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 2 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Use <- again to update x x <- x + 1 x ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 3 ``` ::: ::: ## Names are case-sensitive ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # We already created lowercase y with assignment y ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 6 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # But we have not yet created uppercase Y Y ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error: ! object 'Y' not found ``` ::: ::: ## Finding the right balance ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # rate is allowed but pretty short rate <- 93 rate ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 93 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # heart_rate_in_beats_per_minute is allowed but pretty long heart_rate_in_beats_per_minute <- 93 heart_rate_in_beats_per_minute ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 93 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # heart_rate_bpm might be a nice compromise heart_rate_bpm <- 93 heart_rate_bpm ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 93 ``` ::: ::: ## Be careful of special symbols ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Don't try to add spaces second age <- 12 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error in parse(text = input): :2:8: unexpected symbol 1: # Don't try to add spaces 2: second age ^ ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Don't try to add special symbols age@time2 <- 12 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error: ! object 'age' not found ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Focus on letters, numbers, and underscores age_time2 <- 12 age_time2 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 12 ``` ::: ::: # Functions ## Functions {.fs70} ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column width="60%"} - [Functions]{.b .blue} are like calculator buttons - They let you easily apply a transformation - They can have descriptive names for readability - Is it obvious `x^0.5` is the square root of x? - Is it obvious `sqrt(x)` is the square root of x? ::: {.fragment .mt1} - We may want to combine multiple functions - We *could* use intermediate objects... - But "nested" functions take less room - We resolve nested functions inside-out - Using "pipes" is even better \[04c\] ::: ::: ::: {.column .tc .pv5 width="40%"} {{< lif "../../icons/fn_key.json" trigger=hover colors=secondary:#2a76dd class=rc >}} ::: ::: ## Calling Functions ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Can I turn this into a "button" to press? 9^0.5 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 3 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Take the square root of a number x <- sqrt(9) x ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 3 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Or take the square root of an object y <- sqrt(x) y ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 1.732051 ``` ::: ::: ## Rounding Functions ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Round up ceiling(1 / 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 1 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Round down floor(1 / 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Round to nearest even integer round(0.5) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Round to nearest even integer round(1.5) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 2 ``` ::: ::: ## Other Useful Functions ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Absolute Value abs(-3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 3 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Sign sign(-3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] -1 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Logarithm log(1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Exponential exp(1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 2.718282 ``` ::: ::: ## Basic Trigonometry ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Sine sin(1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.841471 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Cosine cos(1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.5403023 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Tangent tan(1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 1.557408 ``` ::: ::: :::{.fs80} Note: there are corresponding `asin()`, `acos()`, and `atan()` functions. ::: ## Combining Functions ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Using intermediate objects works but takes many lines x <- sqrt(9) y <- cos(x) z <- round(y) z ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] -1 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Alternatively, "nest" them and then resolve inside-out z <- round(cos(sqrt(9))) z ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] -1 ``` ::: :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
